A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same controlled comparison of autoregressive and flow-matching music generation. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, runtime measurements, training-configuration experiments, and a human study of inpainting.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds MusicCaps evaluation, reconstruction measurements, entropy analysis, and further runtime and frame-rate experiments.

M1.justification: The core AR/FM architectures, objectives, representations, temporal conditioning, and inpainting algorithms are retained. FM skip connections already appeared in v1. Removing cross-attention and using argmax in v3 Appendix K are experimental controls, not revisions to the principal methods.

E1.justification: v1 explicitly avoided MusicCaps; v3 evaluates the existing models on it in Appendix F and characterizes its data in Appendix A. This extends evaluation from curated proprietary audio to heterogeneous public recordings while retaining the training sources and core music tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AR, EnCodec-based FM, VAE-based FM, and the supervised/zero-shot inpainting alternatives. MusicCaps reuses the existing comparator set. Appendix F quotes MusicGen's previously reported FAD rather than newly evaluating it.

E3.justification: v3 introduces matched-length/frame-rate experiments, reconstruction evaluation using SI-SNR, ViSQOL and log-MSD, and runtime tests across durations and model depths. Appendix K controls attention and sampling overheads; Appendix I measures entropy over 100 prompts. The revised runtime plot reports batch latency instead of v1's per-sample latency, although the prose remains inconsistent.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial diagnostic evidence: separating sequence-length effects from representation frame rate, checking reconstruction quality, quantifying dataset quality, examining entropy under temporal conditioning, and varying transformer depth to investigate runtime overheads. These extend v1's sampling-step and training-configuration sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: New Appendix A reports CE, PQ and CLAP values with ± quantities across datasets, without defining the dispersion measure. The human study's 95% confidence intervals and approximately 250 judgments per cell remain unchanged; additional training runs or seeds are not reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and the original Euler-sampling results retain their values. v3 adds extensive results, including MusicCaps 25 Hz FAD scores of 4.10 for AR, 5.53 for EnCodec-based FM, and 4.58 for VAE-based FM, plus reconstruction, duration, entropy and model-depth measurements. The runtime throughput curves also change; these should not be interpreted as established same-setting speed improvements.

T1.justification: Section 5.4 adds an approximate runtime derivation using batch size, sequence length, latent dimension, GPU parallelism and FM step count to contrast AR and FM complexity. This is a limited analytical addition; the existing mathematical formulation and algorithms remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central efficiency conclusion changes substantially. v1 emphasizes AR's batch-scaling advantage and FM speed obtained by sacrificing quality; v3's introduction, Table 1 and conclusion emphasize FM's advantage in most tested cases, limiting AR's advantage to large batches and short sequences. The summary also qualifies AR control adherence with accumulated-error susceptibility.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations involving representation compression, conflicting controls and accumulated errors, and possible memory-bandwidth limits on AR inference. It also cautions that adapted representation configurations may be suboptimal and that the observed EnCodec advantage does not establish general superiority. The original 400M-model limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v3 identifies VGGish for FAD and the HTSAT-base CLAP variant, links the backbone configuration, and discloses parameter contributions from skip connections, conditioning projections and embeddings. It also documents controls used in the new runtime ablation. Existing preprocessing, normalization, optimizer settings and inpainting pseudocode are largely retained.

R1.justification: Targeted references and discussion are added for FM–diffusion connections, memory-bound AR inference, dataset selection and architectural choices. The main related-work organization and comparative positioning remain intact. Stable Audio's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The principal section order and much of the original prose remain. v3 makes focused language and explanation edits, reorganizes the conclusion under explicit subheadings, adds a broader-impact paragraph, and renumbers existing appendices around new material. Publication headers are also added.

P2.justification: v3 adds frame-rate/duration, entropy and model-depth/runtime figures, alongside dataset-quality, reconstruction and MusicCaps tables. It redraws the runtime plot with different latency units and batch coverage, and redesigns Table 1 from three columns to two with a limitations row. Several original displays are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the comparison by testing representation-related confounds, adding public-benchmark evidence, and establishing important boundaries on the runtime conclusions. These address weaknesses in v1's evidence and attribution. The gains are tempered by inconsistencies: Section 5.4 retains throughput values that disagree with Figure 5, and Table 7's 100 Hz PQ/CE values disagree with Table 2. These localized problems do not outweigh the stronger diagnostic evidence and more qualified conclusions.
